purpose: Bethanechol is used to help your bladder work properly when it is not emptying on its own. It is often prescribed after surgery or childbirth when the bladder becomes sluggish or weak. It can also help people who have trouble fully emptying their bladder due to certain medical conditions.
how_it_works: Your bladder has muscles that need a chemical signal to squeeze and push urine out. Bethanechol mimics a natural chemical in your body called acetylcholine, which tells those bladder muscles to contract. This helps your bladder squeeze properly so you can urinate more completely and comfortably.
common_side_effects: You may notice nausea, stomach cramps, diarrhea, or an urgent need to urinate. Some people experience flushing, sweating, or a slow heart rate. You might also feel a little dizzy or lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have asthma, a blockage in your bladder or bowel, stomach ulcers, low blood pressure, or certain heart conditions, as it can make these worse. Tell your doctor about all your medications because bethanechol can interact with other drugs. This medicine is taken by mouth only — it should never be injected, as that can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 25 to 50 mg taken by mouth 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor will find the right dose for you. It is best taken on an empty stomach — at least one hour before or two hours after eating — to reduce nausea and stomach upset.
